answer: Lineage Hash Commitment. Each agent must publish a hash chain linking every action to a parent agent's prior hash, forming one continuous lineage. Duplicates cannot fork without producing diverging chains, which any peer can detect by comparing chain tips over a willow relay. The ridge of recorded parent hashes means a copied identity inherits its clone's history and collides. To avoid collision, an attacker must reconstruct a distinct valid lineage per identity, paying full compute and storage for each — a haven of prior work no shortcut can fake.
